claims.claim: This galvanic dissolved oxygen probe consists of an HDPE membrane, an anode bathed in electrolyte and a cathode, and oxygen diffuses through the membrane at a constant rate before being reduced at the cathode to produce a small voltage.

chunks.locator: "How often do you need to recalibrate a dissolved oxygen probe?" through the reconditioning procedure — "0mv – 60+ mv depending on the oxygen saturation"

claims.claim: The galvanic dissolved oxygen probe is a passive device that generates 0 mV to more than 60 mV depending on the oxygen saturation of the sensing membrane, and this voltage can easily be read by a multimeter or an analog-to-digital converter.
claims.quote:
generates a small voltage
from 0mv – 60+ mv depending on the oxygen saturation of the sensing membrane. This
voltage can easily be read by a multimeter or an analog to digital converter.

claims.claim: Atlas Scientific states there is no set recalibration schedule for a dissolved oxygen probe because every use case is different.
claims.quote: Because every use case is different, there is no set schedule for recalibration.

claims.claim: The dissolved oxygen probe consumes its electrolyte solution as it reacts with oxygen, and an industrial dissolved oxygen probe will typically last 2 years before the electrolyte is depleted.
claims.quote:
Typically an industrial
dissolved oxygen probe will last 2 years before the electrolyte is depleted (results will
vary).

claims.claim: When the electrolyte in a dissolved oxygen probe is depleted, the probe reads very low numbers.
claims.quote: When the electrolyte is depleted, the probe will read very low numbers.

claims.claim: Best practice is to replace the electrolyte solution and membrane of the dissolved oxygen probe every 1 to 2 years.
claims.quote:
Best practice is
to replace the electrolyte solution and membrane every 1 – 2 years.

claims.claim: The Gen 3 Industrial DO probe connects either to the EZO Complete-DO and EZO Complete-TMP via its SMA connectors or to the Industrial DO Transmitter, powered at 9-36 VDC, via its tinned leads.
claims.quote: 9 - 36VDC

claims.claim: To add electrolyte solution, unscrew the probe's membrane cap, drain any remaining solution, use the supplied syringe to inject solution into the membrane cap until it is filled half way, screw the cap back on, and rinse the probe.
claims.quote:
Using the supplied syringe, inject solution into
the membrane cap until it's filled half way. Screw the membrane cap back onto probe.

claims.claim: During usage a small amount of zinc oxide corrosion may build up around the anode of the dissolved oxygen probe, causing irregular readings.
claims.quote:
a small amount of corrosion (zinc oxide) may build up around the anode of
the probe, this will cause irregular readings.

claims.claim: To recondition the dissolved oxygen probe, unscrew and drain the membrane cap, file the corrosion buildup off the anode with a small file without filing the cathode, rinse the anode, refill the membrane cap half way with electrolyte and reassemble.
claims.quote:
Using a small file, carefully file off the corrsion buildup
around the anode of the probe. Do not file the cathode, as this will damage the probe.

chunks.locator: "How to replace the membrane cap" through the KCl creep page — "Over time, the membrane can wear out"

claims.claim: Over time the dissolved oxygen probe's membrane wears out, leading to irregular readings, and correcting this requires replacing the membrane cap.
claims.quote:
Over time, the membrane can wear out, this will lead to irregular readings from
the probe. To correct this issue, the probes membrane cap must be replaced.

claims.claim: To replace the membrane cap, unscrew it, drain any remaining electrolyte solution, discard the damaged cap, fill a new membrane cap half way with electrolyte solution and screw it back onto the probe body.
claims.quote:
With a new membrane cap ready, fill the new membrane cap half way with electrolyte
solution and screw back on to probe body.

claims.claim: Soft coatings on a dissolved oxygen probe can be removed by lightly brushing around the sides of the probe and the membrane cap.
claims.quote:
Soft coatings can be removed by lightly brushing around the sides of the probe and
membrane cap.

claims.claim: If the dissolved oxygen probe's membrane needs cleaning, use a mild bleach mixture to gently wash away deposits, and never use a brush on the membrane.
claims.quote:
use a mild bleach mixture
to gently wash away any deposits.
DO NOT USE A BRUSH TO CLEAN THE MEMBRANE

claims.claim: A ripped membrane on the dissolved oxygen probe must be replaced because it causes irregular readings.
claims.quote: If the probes membrane is ripped it must be replaced, as it will cause irregular readings.

claims.claim: If dried KCl residue from the electrolyte solution appears ("KCl creep") or the dissolved oxygen probe dried out during shipping, the probe is not damaged and only needs to be rinsed off with water.
claims.quote:
Simply rinse off your probe with water, and carry on.
Your probe is not damaged.

gaps: Gives no calibration procedure whatsoever: no air/saturated-air calibration step, no zero-solution step, no single- vs two-point sequence, and no calibration standard is named.
States output only in mg/L; gives no percent-saturation output, and no conversion between mg/L and % saturation.
Gives no oxygen solubility table and no barometric-pressure or altitude correction, despite stating that temperature affects the reading.
Gives no salinity correction, even though the probe is rated for salt water and salinity changes oxygen solubility.
States accuracy as +/- 0.05 mg/L with no dependence on temperature, on position in the 0-100 mg/L range, or on membrane age.
Gives no drift rate and no criterion for deciding a reading has drifted; the only failure signal offered is 'reads very low numbers' once electrolyte is depleted.
Names a 60 ml/min flow requirement but gives no method of achieving or verifying it, and no stated error if flow is absent.
Gives no part number or specification for the replacement membrane cap or electrolyte solution, and no volume for a refill beyond 'half way'.
Gives no storage instruction for a probe taken out of service (no storage solution, no wet-storage rule) unlike the pH and ORP datasheets in this set.
Gives no dissolved oxygen values that indicate any water-quality condition — no hypoxia threshold, no healthy range, no environmental interpretation of any kind.
Lists 'No Organic Solvents' as the only chemical contraindication and gives no interference list (e.g. hydrogen sulfide, chlorine) for a galvanic sensor.
summary.notes: Three-chunk document. Chunk 1 opens with ~400 characters of overlap repeating the Specifications/materials block from chunk 0, and chunk 2 opens with overlap repeating the tail of the reconditioning procedure from chunk 1; claims are recorded only on the originating chunk. Two internal tensions worth noting: the spec table gives '~18 Months Maintenance' while the body recommends replacing electrolyte and membrane 'every 1 - 2 years'; and the spec table gives '~1 Year Time before recalibration' while the body says there is no set schedule. This is also the only probe in the set that says its output CAN be read by a multimeter or ADC — the pH and ORP datasheets say the opposite of their own probes. 'Envriomental' and 'corrsion' are spelling errors present in the source text and are preserved verbatim in the quotes. The response-time figure is expressed as a rate (~0.1 mg/L per second), not as a percentage-of-final-value time like the other three probes. The dimensions page arrives as bare numbers with labels detached.
